national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (IRD), acting through the GovHK/eTAX electronic portal, together with the Companies Registry of Hong Kong; where the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture has a mainland China taxable establishment, the State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China remains the competent authority for Corporate Income Tax, VAT, and withholding tax, administered through its electronic tax service platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing or owning the Hong Kong-incorporated JV: first register the private limited liability company at the Companies Registry under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) and obtain the Certificate of Incorporation; if a non-Hong Kong company is used, register it as an overseas company under Part 16 of the Companies Ordinance. Within one month of commencing business in Hong Kong, submit the statutory business registration application to the Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), attaching the incorporation documents, registered office address, director and shareholder particulars, identity proofs, and Hong Kong place of business. The IRD will issue a Business Registration Certificate whose Business Registration Number functions as the Hong Kong tax identification number for profits tax, stamp duty, and employer tax returns. If the JV also establishes a mainland China entity or permanent establishment, the enterprise must first obtain a foreign-invested enterprise business license from the State Administration for Market Regulation, then complete taxpayer registration with the competent State Taxation Administration office under the Tax Administration Law; the Unified Social Credit Code (18-digit) issued at incorporation or registration is the PRC taxpayer identification number and VAT registration identifier. A foreign non-resident shareholder without a mainland permanent establishment does not require a separate PRC TIN solely for withholding on dividends; the PRC payer acts as withholding agent, and a non-resident taxpayer number is assigned only if treaty relief or non-resident business registration is applied for. Hong Kong does not require a VAT/GST identification number because it levies no VAT, GST, or sales tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The CN_JV_LTD is a limited liability corporate vehicle taxed separately from its shareholders; it is not a pass-through entity. In Hong Kong, profits tax is assessed at entity level on profits with a Hong Kong source; in mainland China, a resident foreign-invested enterprise is taxed on worldwide income at entity level under PRC Corporate Income Tax. The default status is therefore Entity_Level_Taxation, with Territorial_Scope principles governing Hong Kong-sourced income only and no tax-exempt-zone pass-through treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Hong Kong's Inland Revenue Ordinance does not provide a check-the-box election; corporations are automatically separate taxpayers. Mainland China also does not offer a U.S.-style check-the-box entity classification; anti-hybrid mismatch rules under the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law operate to deny improper mismatch outcomes. Treaty-based relief under the Mainland-Hong Kong double taxation arrangement is available only by claim and applies to eliminate double taxation, not to reclassify the entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Mainland China Value-Added Tax (VAT) applies to taxable sales, with financial intermediary services generally taxable at 6% and goods at 13%; Hong Kong SAR has no VAT, GST, or Sales and Use Tax. The target HK-incorporated JV is outside the mainland VAT net unless it has a mainland establishment or makes taxable supplies in mainland China.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Hong Kong SAR: none / nil because there is no VAT/GST. Mainland China: mandatory VAT general taxpayer registration is required when annual taxable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000; below that threshold, simplified small-scale taxpayer rules apply unless the taxpayer elects general taxpayer status. The HK-based JV is not required to register for PRC VAT merely for executing the equity crowdfunding platform outside mainland China; registration arises only for mainland taxable activities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Hong Kong SAR: no statutory real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing mandate, or anti-fraud digital stamping regime; commercial invoices and accounting records satisfy Inland Revenue Ordinance record-keeping. Mainland China: VAT invoices and fully digitalized electronic invoices must be issued through the State Taxation Administration's national electronic invoicing and clearance systems, with invoice data transmitted in real time to the tax authorities; the platform applies anti-counterfeit tax control mechanisms, digital stamps, and invoice-existence verification before a mainland VAT taxpayer may claim input VAT credits or export refunds.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For mainland China exports of goods, the statutory criteria are: a genuine cross-border sale to an overseas buyer, physical export of goods from the PRC customs territory under a valid customs declaration, full collection of export proceeds from outside China, and compliance with VAT invoice and export verification requirements. Qualifying cross-border services, including certain fully consumed offshore digital services, may be zero-rated or exempted from PRC VAT if the beneficiary is located outside mainland China, the services are wholly used outside mainland China, and statutory supporting documentation is retained; an equity crowdfunding portal is likely to qualify only for the portion of intermediary services provided and consumed outside mainland China, not for any mainland-regulated activities requiring a financial-services licence. In Hong Kong, no VAT zero-rating is required because Hong Kong imposes no VAT; Hong Kong-sourced profits may still be exempt from profits tax if sourced outside Hong Kong, subject to IRD territorial source rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading (or airway waybill / rail waybill / courier receipt for cross-border goods)
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) / bank foreign exchange receipt certificate
Commercial invoice issued to the overseas customer
Original or digital sales contract or order evidencing the export transaction
Export VAT invoice or zero-rated supply ledger and any export verification report required by the State Taxation Administration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The State Taxation Administration, the General Administration of Customs, and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange jointly scrutinize export zero-rating refund claims. Falsified customs declarations, forged Bills of Lading or FIRCs, unrepatriated export proceeds, or offshore shell transactions trigger retrospective clawback of VAT refunds, late payment surcharges, administrative penalties up to five times the tax involved, disqualification from export tax refund status, VAT invoice controls, and referral for criminal investigation under the PRC Criminal Law for fraudulent export tax refunds. In Hong Kong, false records or fraudulent profits tax claims may lead to IRD estimated assessments, penalties of treble the tax avoided as provided in the Inland Revenue Ordinance, and prosecution; clawback applies to any refund or relief obtained through misrepresentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE); Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) is the banking and monetary authority for Hong Kong SAR.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Hong Kong dollar is fully convertible in a free market under the linked exchange rate system administered by the HKMA; there are no surrender requirements, no approval gates for dividend remittances, and no restrictions on holding foreign currency in Hong Kong. However, the parent company is in mainland China, so any cross-border RMB or FX movement between mainland China and Hong Kong is governed by SAFE. China maintains a managed float and strict capital account controls; current account trade convertibility is generally available once banks verify genuine trade transactions. Capital account flows such as equity subscription by mainland investors into the offshore joint venture, loans, or overseas direct investment require SAFE registration or approval. For an equity crowdfunding portal, the mixture of retail investor money and founder capital increases verification complexity: a bank will characterise each credit individually. Profit remittance from Hong Kong to mainland shareholders is a dividend flow, requiring tax certification and, for mainland resident corporate investors, possibly SAFE balance-of-payments reporting. The practical hurdle is not currency convertibility but compliance-evidence density.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Hong Kong SAR imposes no statutory surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts; all foreign currency may be retained or converted at market rate. For mainland China export-related flows, SAFE requires exporters to repatriate trade proceeds into China and complete trade-monitoring reconciliation. Since the 2012 reform, exporters may voluntarily retain foreign currency earnings and are not subject to mandatory conversion. However, if proceeds are not received within 90 days after the Customs export declaration, the exporter must register a delayed collection filing; otherwise the bank may suspend trade verification. Any export receipt exceeding USD 5 million equivalent remaining unrepatriated beyond 120 days triggers additional SAFE documentary review. The conversion ratio is enterprise-determined and no fixed statute percentage applies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability for the core treasury function. Hong Kong does not grant full banking privileges to offshore electronic money institutions; an entity accepting deposits or conducting money servicing must be authorised under the Banking Ordinance or the Payment Systems and Stored Value Facilities Ordinance. Offshore fintech EMIs such as neobanks and remittance apps are not licensed to hold segregated client escrow for a regulated equity crowdfunding portal. The platform's investor fund custody requirement, segregated trust ledger, and HKMA AML/CFT supervision necessitate a licensed Tier-1 commercial bank as the sole clearing and settlement counterparty. A fintech EMI may only provide ancillary FX conversion or card issuance if it operates through a licensed partner bank, but it cannot be the principal account-holding intermediary and is not recommended for this mandate.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors and all ultimate beneficial owners holding 25% or more must appear physically at the bank's Hong Kong branch for the onboarding interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted for a high-risk special license payer such as an equity crowdfunding portal. Some premier banks permit a hybrid process where a foreign-resident director attends by secure video only after having been previously met by the relationship manager in person; however, the compliance committee will normally require face-to-face interviews with the designated AML compliance officer and at least two directors. Non-Hong Kong directors may provide certified passport copies via the Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office or notary public, but the signature verification interview cannot be delegated to a consular officer for first-see customers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The platform is a non-bank fiduciary that can move third-party investor funds into escrow, creating an automatic higher-risk money laundering and terrorist financing red flag under HKMA AML/CFT guidelines.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the executed trust or escrow custody agreement with a licensed Hong Kong bank, the statutory securities regulator licence for equity crowdfunding, a legal opinion confirming the platform does not operate an unauthorised deposit-taking business, audited segregated escrow ledgers, a real-time investor transaction monitoring protocol, and independent audit certification of the AML control environment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The Sino-Foreign equity joint venture structure blends mainland China shareholders with Hong Kong corporate layers, making source of wealth and business rationale unclear and triggering suspicion of round-trip cross-border financing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the complete corporate ownership chart from mainland parent to Hong Kong entity, SAFE outward direct investment or ODI registration for each mainland shareholder, notarised board resolutions, certified certificates of incumbency, three years of parent company audited financial statements, source-of-funds evidence for the initial capital, and a detailed business plan proving the crowdfunding operations are distinct from depository banking.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Equity crowdfunding receipts may be commingled with founder contribution or unverified subscription fees, producing a laundering pattern of mixed investor funds and unexplained rapid credit turnover.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply the investor suitability and verification procedure for each subscription, a contractual waterfall that releases funds only when a funding round closes, dual-approval escrow release matrices, automated reporting APIs that give the bank read-only access to transaction ledgers, external audit letters over the platform's segregation of accounts, and the named AML compliance officer's professional certification and police clearance certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The purpose of opening a capital escrow account for a niche fintech crowdfunding vehicle is not standard corporate banking activity and may be rejected by the bank's product risk committee as unviable without proof of regulatory standing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: File the official HK licensing or exemption confirmation for ISIC 6499 crowdfunding activity, a schedule of the specific securities laws being relied upon, proof that the platform is not accepting deposits or issuing loans, a FATCA and CRS classification, the statutory auditor's opinion on internal controls over financial reporting, and a default protection or investor compensation arrangement issued by a licensed insurer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Mainland equity injection must flow through the SAFE-registered ODI/ODI framework: the mainland shareholder completes foreign exchange registration with a designated SAFE bank, obtains an overseas direct investment certificate, and remits the capital via SWIFT MT103 using the SAFE capital-account purpose code for overseas direct investment (the 621-family outward direct investment classification). The Hong Kong receiving bank will verify the remitting bank, the ODI certificate, the board resolution, the subscription agreement, and the final share allotment. No statutory capital verification by a Chinese CPA is required in Hong Kong, but the bank will request an audit confirmation letter tying the escrow account balance to issued shares. For non-mainland investors, wire transfers must cite the original source jurisdiction and the business justifications; funds from unrelated third-party payers are prohibited.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational disbursements from the Hong Kong entity must use institutional clearing rails: SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier wires, MT202 COV for bank-to-bank settlement of high-value trade payments, direct RMB clearing through the Hong Kong RMB Clearing House (CHATS) using Bank of China (Hong Kong) as the clearing bank, and confirmed irrevocable documentary letters of credit for large cross-border trade. Commercial documentary collections may be used only when supporting transport and insurance documents are presented through a Tier-1 bank. For disbursements to mainland China, payments should be routed by BOCHK through CIPS and quote the correct SAFE transaction purpose code to avoid rejection. All escrow payouts to invested companies and investor refunds must follow a pre-agreed settlement calendar and be executed through the same bank's corporate electronic banking system with dual-operator token control.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable HKD/USD forward contracts and HKD/RMB forward contracts entered through the Tier-1 treasury desk for hedging operational currency exposure only.
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/CNH or RMB for non-deliverable mainland exposure, requiring full underlying trade or profit remittance documentation.

Currency swaps between HKD and RMB for cross-border principal and interest matching, permitted only after SAFE filing by the mainland counterparty and subject to bank suitability and anti-speculation review.

Interest rate and FX basis swaps linked to actual commercial debt service are permissible, while speculative open positions, crypto-option straddles, and leveraged third-party linked products are expressly forbidden.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (NAR1) under Companies Ordinance section 662
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of incorporation (the return date) for a Hong Kong private limited company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties: HKD 870 if filed more than 42 days but within 3 months; HKD 1,740 within 6 months; HKD 2,610 within 9 months; HKD 3,480 beyond 9 months. Defaulting officers and the company are liable to prosecution and fines; persistent non-filing may lead the Registrar to strike the company off the register and dissolve it under Companies Ordinance section 744.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the expiry date printed on the current Business Registration Certificate; the IRD normally issues a renewal demand approximately one month before the expiry date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to pay by the expiry date incurs an overdue demand fee of HKD 300 and may expose the business to prosecution, a fine of up to HKD 5,000, and imprisonment. Outstanding business registration arrears also block tax clearance and create an enforcement action against the business.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (BIR51) accompanied by audited financial statements and tax reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within one month from the issue date stated on the BIR51, subject to any block extension granted by the IRD for particular financial year-ends and electronic filing arrangements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by the stated deadline gives the IRD the power to raise estimated assessments, imposes late filing penalties up to 10% of the tax undercharged, and may result in prosecution with court fines and additional tax for deliberate or persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pension (BIR56A / BIR56B)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month from the issue date of the employer's return, typically issued in April; exact date is stated on the return and on the IRD publication for the relevant year of assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file without reasonable excuse is an offence under the Inland Revenue Ordinance; on conviction the employer may face a fine and imprisonment, and the court may order additional tax of up to three times the amount undercharged.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: SFC Annual Licence Fee and Submission of Audited Financial Statements and Auditor's Report under the Securities and Futures (Accounts and Audit) Rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), Hong Kong
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual licence fee payable on or before the anniversary of the SFC licence; audited financial statements and the auditor's report must be delivered to the SFC within 4 months after the licensed corporation's financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment of the annual fee may result in suspension or revocation of the licence. Failure to file audited accounts or required financial returns is an offence and can lead to fines, imprisonment for continuing default, regulatory censure, and loss of the licence; it is not a strike-off trigger but it terminates the regulated electronic crowdfunding activity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting and Presentation of Audited Financial Statements to Members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company members and statutory auditor of the Hong Kong company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a private company, the annual general meeting must be held within 9 months after the end of the accounting reference period; audited financial statements must be laid before the members at the meeting or, if the AGM is dispensed with by unanimous written resolution, circulated to every member with the auditor's report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors are liable on conviction to fines for failure to hold the AGM or lay the financial statements before members; where this is combined with failure to file annual returns, the Companies Registry may treat the company as not carrying on business and initiate administrative strike-off action.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Hong Kong does not impose quantitative balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount thresholds that create a mandatory audit obligation; all active Hong Kong companies must be audited under Companies Ordinance Cap 622 section 359 unless dormant or in a narrow small-company exemption. For context, the small private company audit exemption conceptually applies to a company satisfying at least two of three de minimis criteria: annual revenue not exceeding HKD 25 million, total assets not exceeding HKD 25 million, and not more than 25 employees; such a company may also need unanimous member consent. However, a licensed equity crowdfunding portal regulated by the SFC is a licensed corporation and cannot rely on any small-company or audit exemption. The SFC's Securities and Futures (Accounts and Audit) Rules require mandatory independent certified CPA audits of the licensed entity at all times regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants, which are substantially aligned with IFRS; HKFRS for Private Entities may be used only by eligible non-public-interest private entities and is not available to an SFC-licensed corporation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong has no separate annual UBO confirmation filing to the Companies Registry. Under Companies Ordinance Cap 622 section 653, the Significant Controllers Register (equivalent to a UBO register) must be maintained at the registered office or an elected location and updated within 7 days of any change. The company must take reasonable steps to identify significant controllers and serve notices requiring information within 7 days of becoming aware of a new controller. The Annual Return (NAR1) confirms only the company's members and capital structure at the return date; it does not confirm beneficial ownership. As an SFC-licensed equity crowdfunding portal, ongoing FATF-aligned AML/CFT customer due diligence and beneficial ownership records must also be maintained for the SFC.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Members and Directors Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 1,800 per annum for registered office address, correspondence handling, and corporate secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 per annum for a licensed equity crowdfunding portal requiring SFC-compliant audit procedures, financial resources rule review, and special regulatory reporting

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 16.5% (Hong Kong Profits Tax on corporations; 8.25% on the first HKD 2,000,000 of assessable profits under the two-tiered profits tax rate regime for qualifying corporations)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial source income taxation with foreign-source income exemption; no capital gains tax; no dividend withholding tax; two-tiered profits tax concession; 100% first-year initial allowance and annual allowances on qualifying capital expenditure on plant and machinery; qualifying R&D expenditure deduction at 300% for the first HKD 2 million and 200% on the remainder; no patent box or free-zone tax holiday, but specific concessions apply to aviation leasing, marine shipping, reinsurance, specialist funds and qualifying debt instruments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form BIR51 - Profits Tax Return for Corporations (Inland Revenue Department), filed electronically through the IRD eTax / eFiling portal; audited financial statements and tax computation schedules are submitted as supporting documents.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (Hong Kong Year of Assessment: 1 April to 31 March)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The BIR51 must generally be filed within 1 month from the date of issue by the IRD; with an appointed Hong Kong tax representative and eTax filing authorization, the IRD routinely extends the deadline by accounting year-end: for a 31 December year-end, generally to 15 August; for a 31 March year-end, generally to 15 November; and for other basis periods, to the IRD-published extended due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business name, Business Registration (BR) number, registered office and principal place of business, industry code (ISIC 6499 / HKISIC for other financial service activities not elsewhere classified).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact legal name and BR number of the Hong Kong-incorporated Sino-Foreign Joint Venture. For a non-resident-controlled entity, clearly identify the Hong Kong place of management and control, the address where board decisions are made, and the location of executive directors and key compliance staff. Avoid nominee-only addresses as this will weaken tax residence and treaty claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Basis period start and end dates, first return indicator, and Hong Kong tax residency declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare whether the company is a Hong Kong tax resident only by reason of incorporation or by other tie-breaker factors. If central management and control is actually exercised in Mainland China, the company may be treated as PRC tax resident under the Mainland-Hong Kong Arrangement; this must be disclosed and contemporaneous board minutes, meeting attendances and physical locations must support the Hong Kong residence position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Turnover: gross commissions, success fees, subscription fees, investor matching fees, due diligence facilitation fees, escrow and payment-processing revenues from the equity crowdfunding portal.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all gross portal income. Hong Kong territorial source taxation applies only to profits arising in or derived from Hong Kong. The IRD will treat fees arising from the crowdfunding arrangement activities performed, managed and controlled in Hong Kong as chargeable. An offshore claim is unlikely to succeed if the portal infrastructure, negotiation, contract execution, AML/KYC functions, IT servers and fund custody are located in Hong Kong merely because the investors or issuers are in Mainland China.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Other income: bank interest, escrow interest, management fees, government subsidies, foreign exchange gains, and miscellaneous operating income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all ancillary income. Escrow interest received in connection with the Hong Kong regulated crowdfunding business is generally Hong Kong-source and chargeable. Foreign-source interest or offshore income should only be excluded if the underlying lending/escrow activity is performed outside Hong Kong and the relevant payments are received outside Hong Kong; provide a detailed source computation if such an exclusion is claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses and costs: staff salaries, rental and premises costs, information technology infrastructure, cybersecurity, AML/KYC compliance software, licensing and regulatory fees, professional advisory fees, marketing and investor communication expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim deductions only where incurred wholly and exclusively in the production of chargeable profits under IRO section 16. For an equity crowdfunding portal, SFC licensing fees, legal structuring costs, due diligence database costs, insurance premiums and AML screening tools are deductible. Capitalised software development expenditure must not be expensed through the profit and loss account; instead claim capital allowances where eligible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss per audited financial statements, adjusted by adding back tax-disallowable expenditure and subtracting capital allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Start from accounting net profit. Add back accounting depreciation, entertainment expenses, fines, penalties, donations, non-business expenses, and provisions not permitted under the IRO. Deduct tax depreciation called capital allowances (initial and annual allowances). If the JV exports capital or services to the Mainland shareholder, any amount incorrectly treated as deductible royalty or management fee must be tested against the arm's length principle before being reflected in the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital allowances: initial allowance (IA) at 60%, annual allowances (AA) on plant and machinery, computer hardware, software, servers and crowdfunding platform equipment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim initial and annual allowances on qualifying capital expenditure incurred and used to produce chargeable profits. Computer hardware, servers, network equipment and certain qualifying software platform assets qualify for capital allowances. Assets supplied free of charge by a connected non-resident parent may require transfer pricing valuation; do not claim allowances without documentary evidence of true economic ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessable profits or adjusted losses before loss relief, including the foreign-source income exclusion schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the offshore claims schedule only where the JV can demonstrate that essential profit-generating activities - negotiation, final decision-making, performance and implementation of the crowdfunding portal contracts - took place outside Hong Kong. For a regulated equity crowdfunding portal with Hong Kong market authorisation, the IRD will likely reject the offshore claim if clients are onboarded, compliance is centrally managed, and contracts are concluded in Hong Kong. The burden is on the taxpayer to prove that profits are not Hong Kong-source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss relief: trading losses brought forward from previous years to be set off against current year assessable profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Hong Kong permits an unlimited carry-forward of business losses for a continuing trade. The JV must maintain unbroken continuity of the same business; a major shareholding change combined with a cessation of the crowdfunding trade may extinguish the losses. Losses from unlicensed financial activity periods are not deductible if the business was conducted illegally.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident and related-party declaration: whether any profits are attributable to a permanent establishment in Mainland China or another jurisdiction; related-party transaction schedule; beneficial ownership of the company's shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all related-party transactions with the PRC parent or affiliates, including technology licensing, management fees, escrow administration, data-sharing and royalty payments. The return must be accompanied by a transfer pricing summary sufficient to show that cross-border intercompany charges are at arm's length. The BIR51 does not compute PRC withholding tax, but the dividend declaration minutes and Hong Kong tax residency certificate must be ready to substantiate the 5% treaty withholding rate on any PRC subsidiary dividend repatriation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signed declaration by director or company secretary certifying that the return is complete, true, correct and accompanied by the audited financial statements and tax computations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The director signing the BIR51 assumes personal responsibility for the accuracy of all statements. Delegating preparation to a tax representative does not transfer criminal liability. Deliberately signing an incorrect return with a false offshore claim or inflated deduction exposes the director to criminal prosecution under the Inland Revenue Ordinance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incorrect filing without reasonable excuse: IRO section 80(2) - a fine of up to HKD 10,000 plus additional tax of up to three times the undercharged tax; IRO section 82A - an additional assessment of up to 10% of the undercharged tax for failure to file or submission of an incorrect return; the IRD may also raise estimated assessments and refuse extensions. Wilful tax evasion with intent to defraud: IRO section 82(1) - fine of HKD 50,000 and imprisonment for up to 3 years plus additional tax of up to 100% of the tax undercharged. Directors who consent to or connive in the filing of false returns may be prosecuted personally.
